newsitem.title: USA: Arafat says he would arrest killers of land dealers.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says he would arrest killers of land dealers.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said he is "absolutely against" vigilante executions of Palestinians who sell land to Israelis, and added that those responsible would be arrested if they were found.
"We are absolutely against anyone taking the law into his own hands," Arafat said in an interview in the current issue of Newsweek magazine, which goes on sale on Monday.
Three Arabs have been "executed without trial" since Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen was quoted on May 4 as saying Palestinians who sold land to Jews faced execution.

The PLO said it was activating a Jordanian military law -- banning the sale of land to Israelis on penalty of death -- because the measure was necessary to prevent Jewish settlement building in the Gaza Strip and West Bank, including Israeli-annexed East Jerusalem.
In the Newsweek interview, conducted on Friday, Arafat said, "The death penalty hasn't been carried out and never will be." He said the three Arabs were killed "by unknown persons."
Israeli police have said they are holding at least four Palestinian security officials believed to have been involved in the killings.
Arafat was asked about Israeli intelligence implicating the head of one of his security services in the murders.
"It is not right, not true completely," Arafat said.
Asked if he would arrest those responsible, Arafat said, "Definitely. If we find them, we will arrest them."
Arafat was also asked if there were danger that Palestinians would resort to violence due to frustration at the stalled peace negotiations with Israel.

The two sides reached an impasse last March when Israel started work on a new Jewish settlement at an Arab East Jerusalem site which Israel calls Har Homa and Palestinians refer to as Jabal Abu Ghneim.
"Patience has its limits," Arafat said. "People are beginning to ask, 'Why are you the only partner paying the price of the peace?'. Desperation leads to desperate acts."
He added that he would like to see more and higher-level U.S. involvement in the peace negotiations.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators met in Cairo on Sunday for the first time in more than two months, aiming to revive the stalled peace process.
